block.prompt:
The programme now lets four people with very different stakes sum up their view in one sentence. Listen twice, then match each voice (1–4) to the opinion (A–E) that best fits it. One opinion is NOT needed.

[Your teacher reads:]
1. (a hotel owner) “Tourism pays for everything here — the school bus, the doctor, the shops. Without visitors, this village would simply die.”
2. (a young resident) “I grew up here, but I can't afford a flat here any more. The whole place has become a museum that I'm not allowed to live in.”
3. (a tour guide) “The problem isn't the NUMBER of people, it's how they behave. A little respect — keeping the noise down, not blocking doorways — would change everything.”
4. (a day visitor) “I've got one day and a long list of places to see. I feel a bit guilty, but honestly I'll probably never come back, so I just want the photo.”

right: A — The village could not survive financially without its visitors.
B — The real problem is not how many tourists come, but how they behave.
C — Local people are being priced out of their own home town.
D — Visitors should be forced to pay a much higher entry fee.
E — Time pressure makes a visitor treat the place as just a photo stop.

block.answer_key: 1–A, 2–C, 3–B, 4–E. Opinion D is the distractor — nobody in this clip calls for a higher entry fee (a fee was only mentioned earlier, about Venice).
watch_outs: D ist ein bewusster Distraktor: Weil im Intro (t1) eine Gebühr in Venedig vorkam, wählen manche D vorschnell. Darauf hinweisen, dass in DIESEM Ausschnitt niemand eine Gebühr fordert.
Voice 3 sagt ausdrücklich ‚isn't the NUMBER of people' — wer nur ‚people/number' hört, ordnet leicht falsch zu. Auf die Verneinung achten.
Sicherstellen, dass die vier Stimmen mit erkennbar unterschiedlicher Sprechhaltung vorgelesen werden — das ist die eigentliche Hörleistung.
